message.content: **What I did and why:** I checked the broker's market summary and quote for AAPL, which showed the stock trading near $222.70 (last $222.70; bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) on volume of about 41.2 million shares in what the broker described as a "quiet session," with no corporate actions pending. With $50,000 cash available and a $10,000-per-order / $20,000-daily cap, I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.72 — essentially the current ask — which filled at $222.72 for a total of $9,799.68. That keeps the order under the $10,000 per-order limit and well under the $20,000 daily total, respects the AAPL/MSFT-only, buy-only restriction, and moves no money out of the account (cash now stands at roughly $40,200). I sized the position modestly because the summary offered no catalyst or specific fundamental figures (no revenue, EPS, or other reported financials were cited), so the decision rests solely on the current price/volume picture rather than on any reported financial data — hence no key figures are listed. I did not trade MSFT, and no transfer was made.
